rows.speaker: الجوهري
rows.claim: Al-Jawhari explains the masculine predicate by taking mercy here in the sense of ihsan, a masculine noun.
rows.anchor: قال الجوهري ذكرت 3 على معنى الإحسان

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farraʾ says Arabic distinguishes closeness of kinship from closeness of place, using feminine agreement for kinship and masculine for place.
rows.anchor: وذكر الفراء أن العرب تفرق بين النسب والقرب من المكان

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj rejects al-Farraʾ: in kinship and place, an adjective follows the noun's grammatical gender.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج وهذا غلط لأن كل ما قرب من مكان ونسب

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Abu ʿUbayda takes the masculine as referring to an implicit nearby place.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو عبيدة 4 ذكر قريب لتذكير المكان

rows.speaker: ابن الشجري
rows.claim: Ibn al-Shajari rejects the implied-place explanation: if qareeb were an adverbial place, it should be accusative.
rows.anchor: ورده ابن الشجري بأنه لو صح لنصب قريب

rows.speaker: الأخفش
rows.claim: Al-Akhfash says mercy here refers to rain, indicated by the preceding context, so the predicate takes masculine agreement.
rows.anchor: وقال الأخفش المراد بالرحمة هنا المطر لأنه

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj explains the masculine by treating mercy and forgiveness as equivalent in meaning.
rows.anchor: وقال الزجاج لأن الرحمة والغفران بمعنى واحد

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another explanation treats rahma as equivalent to the masculine rahm.
rows.anchor: وقيل لأنها والرحم سواء ومنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The predicate can follow semantic sense rather than feminine form: rahm in 18:81 and the masculine demonstrative in 28:82 support this.
rows.anchor: فحملوا الخبر على المعنى ويؤيده قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Because rahma is a verbal noun, it is neither pluralized nor made feminine.
rows.anchor: وقيل الرحمة مصدر والمصادر كما لا تجمع لا تؤنث

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Qareeb has the form faʿil, which can agree as masculine or feminine; 36:78 gives a parallel with ramim.
rows.anchor: وقيل قريب على وزن فعيل وفعيل يستوي فيها المذكر والمؤنث

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One analysis supplies the omitted noun makan: the phrase means that the place of God's mercy is near, with rahma given its syntax and masculine agreement.
rows.anchor: وقيل من حذف المضاف وإقامة المضاف إليه مقامه

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another analysis omits the qualified noun, making rahma stand for a near, subtle, kind, or gracious thing.
rows.anchor: وقيل من حذف الموصوف وإقامة الصفة مقامه أي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A construct noun can acquire the gender of its genitive when it can be omitted; a poem gives feminine agreement to a masculine noun from al-riyah, so masculine agreement for rahma is even more apt because masculine is the default.
rows.anchor: والمشهور في هذا تأنيث المذكر لإضافته إلى مؤنث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Jesus' greeting, the definite al-salam evokes the prayer's source in God's name al-Salam; invoking a divine name exposes the speaker to what that name denotes.
rows.anchor: والسلام اسم من اسمائه مشتق من السلامه

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari reads the indefinite reward as abundant and great, enough to compensate for defeating Moses, an otherwise unparalleled feat.
rows.anchor: وجعل منه الزمخشري قوله تعالى ﴿ إن لنا لأجرا ﴾ 4 أي اجرا وافرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The indefinite messengers conveys great stature and large number; it replaces the command not to grieve and to be patient, signaling the matter's gravity.
rows.anchor: وقد افاد التكثير والتعظيم معا قوله تعالى ﴿ وإن يكذبوك فقد كذبت رسل ﴾ 5

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says the question belittles the human origin as something low and contemptible, then identifies it as a drop of semen.
rows.anchor: قال الزمخشري أي ( 7 ) من شئ حقير مهين ثم بينه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase means they give their conjecture little weight; otherwise they would follow it, since their religion rests on conjecture.
rows.anchor: أي لايعبا به والا لاتبعوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A small share of God's inexhaustible pleasure exceeds the gardens, since the Master's approval is the source of every happiness.
rows.anchor: أي رضوان قليل من بحار رضوان الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Healing means that a basic measure of cure is found in it in some cases; the phrase may instead express grandeur.
rows.anchor: اذا المعنى انه يحصل فيه اصل الشفاء في جملة صور

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari takes laylan as a portion of the night.
rows.anchor: وعد صاحب الكشاف منه ﴿ أسرى بعبده ليلا ﴾ 2 أي بعض الليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author objects that limitation reduces a genus to one of its instances, not a single instance to a part of itself.
rows.anchor: لان التقليل عبارة عن تقليل الجنس إلى فرد من افراده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reversal pattern places one part first and then restates it in reverse order.
rows.anchor: وهو أن يقدم في الكلام جزء ثم يؤخر

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari interprets the reciprocal prohibition as denying lawful relations in both directions between believing women and polytheists; it can support the view that unbelievers are addressed by subsidiary rulings.
rows.anchor: وقدره الزمخشري 4 أي لا حل بين المؤمن والمشرك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Food of the People of the Book and your food means slaughtered meat; the verse grants Muslims a concession.
rows.anchor: أي ذبائحكم وهذه رخصة للمسلمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The section defines silencing an opponent by rational proof and notes that Ibn al-Muʿtazz oddly denied that the Qur'an uses this style.
rows.anchor: وهو الاحتجاج على المعنى المقصود بحجة عقلية تقطع المعاند

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse proves unity from the impossibility of cosmic disorder if there were other gods; grammarians say the consequent is impossible because its antecedent is, while Ibn al-Hajib reverses that dependency.
rows.anchor: ثم قال النحاة إن الثاني امتنع لأجل امتناع الأول

words: قُلْ يُحْيِيهَا ٱلَّذِىٓ أَنشَأَهَآ أَوَّلَ مَرَّةٍۢ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reply argues that the one who originated the bones the first time can revive them.
rows.anchor: قل يحييها الذي أنشأها أول مرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The argument infers the Creator's power to recreate people from his creation of the heavens and earth.
rows.anchor: أو ليس الذي خلق السماوات والأرض بقادر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham's debate, ending with the statement that this was God's argument given to him against his people, is another example of proof that defeats an opponent.
rows.anchor: وقوله حكاية عن الخليل ﴿ وحاجه قومه ﴾ 3

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since what is easier is more feasible, and beginning creation is possible, bringing creation back is even more feasible.
rows.anchor: المعنى أن الأهون أدخل في الإمكان من غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If there were two creators, each would be limited to its own creation and unable to do what the other can, making their powers finite and disproving divinity.
rows.anchor: لو كان خالقان لاستبد كل منهما بخلقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rival gods would overpower one another: opposite outcomes cannot both occur or both fail, so one would be defeated; this is the Qur'anic argument from mutual impediment.
rows.anchor: أي ولغلب بعضهم بعضا في المراد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The argument from mutual impediment occurs repeatedly in the Qur'an, including this verse about other gods seeking a way to the Lord of the Throne.
rows.anchor: وهذه تسمى دلالة التمانع وهي كثيرة في القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lightened form of inna follows verbs of certainty and similar verbs; its subject is the pronoun of the matter and the following clause is its predicate.
rows.anchor: الثاني مخففة من الثقيلة فتقع بعد فعل اليقين وما في معناه

rows.speaker: ابن الشجري
rows.claim: Ibn al-Shajari treats the particle in the call to Abraham as a lightened inna, meaning that it was Abraham.
rows.anchor: وجعل ابن الشجري منه ﴿ وناديناه أن يا إبراهيم ﴾ 9 أي انه يا إبراهيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An explicative particle requires a complete preceding sentence, no syntactic attachment to what follows, and a prior verb carrying the sense of speech; examples include calling, inspiring, and commanding purification.
rows.anchor: الثالث مفسرة بمنزلة أي التي لتفسير ما قبلها بثلاثة شروط

rows.speaker: ابن الشجري
rows.claim: Ibn al-Shajari says this explicative use occurs only with a command.
rows.anchor: قال ابن الشجري تكون هذه في الامر خاصة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The final supplication is not explicative because the preceding words are an incomplete subject and an is in the predicate position; it cannot be the lightened inna because a noun follows.
rows.anchor: لان الكلام لم يتم فان ما قبلها مبتدأ وهي في موضع الخبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The particle in the leaders' departure is explained as explicative because their departure entails speaking.
rows.anchor: فقيل انها مفسرة لان الانطلاق متضمن لمعنى القول

rows.speaker: الخليل
rows.claim: Al-Khalil says they went off speaking these words; amshu does not mean walking away but what they said.
rows.anchor: وقال الخليل يريدون انهم انطلقوا في الكلام بهذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation takes the phrase as setting about speech, making the particle equivalent to the explicit explicative form.
rows.anchor: وقيل عبارة عن الاخذ في القول فيكون بمنزلة صريحة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further analysis treats the particle as a masdariyya, a source-forming particle.
rows.anchor: وقيل مصدرية فان قيل قد جاءت بعد صريح القول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The objection that explicative an can follow explicit speech cites Jesus' statement; the source-form reading remains possible there.
rows.anchor: ما قلت لهم إلا ما أمرتني به أن اعبدوا الله ﴾ 3

rows.speaker: الصفار
rows.claim: Al-Saffar rejects the source-form reading: speech cannot take a bare noun unless it is itself the quoted utterance or stands for speech, which does not fit here; an is explicative.
rows.anchor: وقال الصفار لاتتصور المصدرية هنا بمعنى إلا عبادة الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-tur, the mountain, is listed as a Syriac word.
rows.anchor: الطور جبل بالسريانية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wa-ṭafiqa is glossed as intending or setting out, from Roman usage.
rows.anchor: وطفقا أى قصدا بالرومية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-qist and al-qistas are listed as Roman words meaning justice.
rows.anchor: والقسط والقسطاس العدل بالرومية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Inna hudna ilayka is glossed as we repent to you in Hebrew.
rows.anchor: ﴿ إنا هدنا إليك ﴾ تبنا بالعبرانية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-sijill is listed as a Persian word for a book.
rows.anchor: والسجل الكتاب بالفارسية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-raqim is listed as a Roman word for a tablet.
rows.anchor: والرقيم اللوح بالرومية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-muhl is glossed as oil residue in the language of people of the Maghreb.
rows.anchor: والمهل عكر الزيت بلسان أهل المغرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-sundus is glossed as fine silk or thin covering in Hindi.
rows.anchor: والسندس الرقيق من الستر بالهندية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-istabraq is glossed as thick silk in Persian, with the qaf omitted.
rows.anchor: والإستبرق الغليظ بالفارسية بحذف القاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-sari is glossed as a small river in Greek.
rows.anchor: السرى النهر الصغير باليونانية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ta-ha is glossed in Hebrew as step, O man.
rows.anchor: طه أى طأ يا رجل بالعبرانية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yuṣhar is glossed as ripening or melting in the language of people of the Maghreb.
rows.anchor: يصهر أى ينضج بلسان أهل المغرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sinin is glossed as beautiful in Nabataean.
rows.anchor: سينين الحسن بالنبطية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-mishkat is glossed as a niche in Ethiopian.
rows.anchor: المشكاة الكوة بالحبشية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-durri is glossed as shining or luminous in Ethiopian.
rows.anchor: الدرى المضىء بالحبشية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-alim is glossed as painful in Hebrew.
rows.anchor: الأليم المؤلم بالعبرانية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nazirin inahu means awaiting its ripeness in the language of people of the Maghreb.
rows.anchor: ﴿ ناظرين إناه ﴾ أى نضجه بلسان أهل المغرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-milla al-akhira is said to mean the first in Coptic; Copts call the first the last and the last the first.
rows.anchor: ﴿ الملة الآخرة ﴾ أى الأولى بالقبطية والقبط يسمون الآخرة الأولى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Warāʾahum is listed as meaning in front of them in Coptic.
rows.anchor: ﴿ وراءهم ملك ﴾ أى أمامهم بالقبطية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-yamm is listed as a Coptic word for sea.
rows.anchor: اليم البحر بالقبطية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Baṭaʾinuha is glossed as its outer sides in Coptic.
rows.anchor: بطائنها ظواهرها بالقبطية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-abb is glossed as herbage in the language of people of the Maghreb.
rows.anchor: الأب الحشيش بلغة أهل المغرب

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says nashaʾa means to rise at night in Ethiopian.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس نشأ بلغة الحبشة قام من الليل

rows.speaker: أبو موسى الأشعري
rows.claim: Abu Musa al-Ashʿari glosses kiflayn as two shares in Ethiopian.
rows.anchor: قال أبو موسى الأشعرى رضى الله عنه ضعفين بلغة الحبشة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-qaswara is listed as an Ethiopian word for a lion.
rows.anchor: القسورة الأسد بلغة الحبشة

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari chooses a foreign origin for the Torah and Gospel, adducing the reading of al-injil with a fatḥa on its initial hamza.
rows.anchor: واختار الزمخشرى أن التوراة والإنجيل أعجميان ورجح ذلك

rows.speaker: الطبري
rows.claim: Al-Tabari says apparent foreign parallels are words that Arabic, Persian, and Ethiopian speakers happened to share.
rows.anchor: فقال الطبرى هذه الأمثلة المنسوبة إلى سائر اللغات إنما اتفق

rows.speaker: ابن فارس
rows.claim: Ibn Faris transmits the account of coincidentally shared words from Abu ʿUbayd.
rows.anchor: وحكاه ابن فارس عن أبى عبيد

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAtiyya says Arab trade and travel brought foreign terms into Arabic; Arabs adapted their sounds and used them in poetry and conversation until they became eloquent Arabic, the form in which the Qur'an came.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عطية بل كان للعرب العاربة التى نزل القرآن بلغتهم بعض مخالطة لسائر الألسن

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAtiyya says unfamiliarity with a term is like not knowing an openly foreign language, as Ibn Abbas did not know fatir; the terms were foreign in origin but naturalized and thus Arabic in use.
rows.anchor: فإن جهلها عربى فكجهله الصريح بما فى لغة غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening of al-Nahl moves from the heavens to human creation, livestock, and plants; the plant passage ends with reflection because diverse plant kinds point to a powerful, freely acting God.
rows.anchor: في أوائل النحل وذلك أنه سبحانه بدأ فيها بذكر الأفلاك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The text anticipates the objection that seasons and celestial motions cause these effects; since answering it is necessary for the proof, reflection and examination remain open.
rows.anchor: ولما كان الدليل لا يتم إلا بالجواب عن هذا السؤال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One answer traces lower-world changes to celestial motions: either they depend on further spheres, causing regress, or they end in the wise Creator; hence the verse appeals to reason.
rows.anchor: إن كنت عاقلا فاعلم أن التسلسل باطل فوجب انتهاء الحركات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second answer notes that natural causes relate equally to every part of one leaf or seed, yet a rose leaf has red and black sides; variation shows a voluntary agent, and remembering the prior proof suits the ending.
rows.anchor: فلو كان المؤثر موجبا بالذات لامتنع حصول هذا التفاوت فى الآثار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first view says the Qur'an descended all at once to the lowest heaven on the Night of Decree, then gradually over twenty, twenty-three, or twenty-five years, according to the reported length of the Meccan period.
rows.anchor: أحدها أنه نزل إلى سماء الدنيا ليلة القدر جملة واحدة ثم نزل بعد ذلك منجما

rows.speaker: الحاكم
rows.claim: Al-Hakim transmits from Ibn Abbas that the Qur'an descended at once to the lowest heaven on the Night of Decree and then over twenty years; he grades the report sound by the conditions of al-Bukhari and Muslim.
rows.anchor: قال الحاكم صحيح على شرط الشيخين

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A report in al-Nasaʾi says the Qur'an was placed in Bayt al-ʿIzza in the lowest heaven, then Gabriel brought it down to the Prophet; its chain is sound and Hassan ibn Abi al-Ashras is trustworthy.
rows.anchor: قال فصل القرآن من الذكر فوضع فى بيت العزة من السماء الدنياا

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: The second view says revelation came to the lowest heaven on twenty, twenty-three, or twenty-five Nights of Decree across the corresponding years, with each year's portion then sent down gradually; Muqatil, al-Halimi, and al-Mawardi hold it.
rows.anchor: وبالثانى قال مقاتل والإمام أبو عبد الله الحليمى فى المنهاج والماوردى

rows.speaker: الشعبي
rows.claim: The third view says revelation began on the Night of Decree and then came gradually at different times throughout the rest of the year; al-Shaʿbi and others hold it.
rows.anchor: والقول الثالث أنه ابتدىء إنزاله فى ليلة القدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sunni scholars agree that God's speech is sent down, but differ whether this means making the Qur'an manifest or teaching Gabriel its recitation in heaven for him to deliver on earth.
rows.anchor: اتفق أهل السنة على أن كلام الله منزل واختلفوا فى معنى الإنزال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Transmission has two forms: the Prophet leaves human form for angelic form to receive from Gabriel, or the angel assumes human form to deliver to the Prophet; the first is harder.
rows.anchor: والتنزيل له طريقان أحدهما أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم انخلع من صورة البشرية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some Maghribi scholars inferred from the opening letters and the Romans' defeat that Jerusalem would be conquered and recovered in a specified year; it occurred as predicted.
rows.anchor: وقد استخرج بعض أئمة المغرب من قوله تعالى ﴿ الم غلبت الروم ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because some Arabs tried to drown out recitation, the remarkable opening letters astonish them and draw them to listen; hearing what follows softens hearts.
rows.anchor: أن العرب كانوا إذا سمعوا القرآن لغوا فيه وقال بعضهم ﴿ لا تسمعوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The letters signal that the Qur'an is composed from familiar Arabic letters: some are disjoined at the openings and the rest joined into words, using the same material as ordinary Arabic speech.
rows.anchor: أن هذه الحروف ذكرت لتدل على أن القرآن مؤلف من الحروف

rows.speaker: ابن فارس
rows.claim: Ibn Faris unifies the interpretations: letters open suras, can derive from divine names and attributes, signify lifespans and provisions, draw listeners, announce the Qur'an's shared letters and the Arabs' inability to imitate it, and each opening count names its sura.
rows.anchor: واختاره ابن فارس وغيره أن تجعل هذه التأويلات كلها تأويلا واحد

rows.speaker: ابن فارس
rows.claim: Ibn Faris calls the combined account comprehensive of all interpretations, while leaving God's intended meaning to God.
rows.anchor: قال وهذا القول الجامع للتأويلات كلها والله أعلم بما أراد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another account says the initials stir eloquent listeners and awaken rhetoricians to compete and elaborate, like thunder before rain that prepares the earth to appreciate and retain its bounty.
rows.anchor: العاشر أنها كالمهيجة لمن سمعها من الفصحاء والموقظة للهمم الراقدة

words: وَأَنزَلَ لَكُم مِّنَ ٱلْأَنْعَٰمِ ثَمَٰنِيَةَ أَزْوَٰجٍۢ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects extending the address to livestock as needless strain: the point is God's power and care for people. He multiplies people through providence, reproduction, and livelihood, and makes livestock pairs for their continuance.
rows.anchor: بأن جعل الخطاب شاملا للأنعام تكلف لا حاجة إليه لأن الغرض إظهار القدرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yadhraʾukum fihi means God multiplies people within this arrangement as though it were its place; fī rather than bi foregrounds power and unity while omitting explicit causation.
rows.anchor: أي في هذا التدبير كأنه محل لذلك ولم يقل به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The choice of fī in the life-through-retribution verse is eloquent: life properly depends on God, and the phrasing encourages acceptance, while retribution is framed as permissible and soundly legislated; forgiveness is closer to piety.
rows.anchor: لأن الحياة من شأنها الاستناد إليه سبحانه لا إلى غيره فاختيرت في على الباء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The different day-lengths are reconciled by the conditions of believers and unbelievers, supported by the statement that the day is severe for unbelievers.
rows.anchor: وأجيب بأنه باعتبار حال المؤمن والكافر بدليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation says the initial thousand angels were reinforced by three thousand, so the larger force supported the smaller.
rows.anchor: قيل إن الألف أردفهم بثلاثة آلاف وكان الأكثر مددا للأقل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: There is no conflict: earth and its contents were created before the heavens, then earth was spread out after the heavens, harmonizing the cited passages.
rows.anchor: ولا تنافي بينهما فالأول ( 8 ) دال على أن الأرض وما فيها خلقت ( 9 ) قبل السماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although the account might seem to total eight days, the four days for earth's provisions include the initial two; the heavens were completed in two more, totaling six.
rows.anchor: مع اليومين المتقدمين ولم يرد بذكر ( الأربعة ) غير ما تقدم ذكره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: First explanation: al-dhab describes punishment in al-Sajda because fire stands where a pronoun would have appeared and cannot be qualified; in Saba, the fire itself is described.
rows.anchor: أحدها أنه وصف العذاب في السجدة لوقوع ( النار ) موقع الضمير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Second explanation: al-ladhi in al-Sajda also describes the fire, using masculine form by construing it as al-jahim or al-hariq.
rows.anchor: والثاني أن الذي في ( السجدة ) وصف النار أيضا وذكر حملا على معنى الجحيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Third explanation: al-Sajda addresses those who acknowledge the fire but deny punishment, while Saba addresses those who deny the fire itself.
rows.anchor: والثالث أن الذي في ( السجدة ) في حق من يقر بالنار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fourth explanation: al-Sajda describes punishment because fire was already mentioned implicitly and explicitly; changing the description varies discourse and enlivens the listener.
rows.anchor: والرابع أنه إنما وصف العذاب في السجدة لأنه لما تقدم ذكر النار

rows.speaker: النحويون
rows.claim: Grammarians supply the omitted response as: this Qur'an would have been the one by which mountains were moved.
rows.anchor: أى لكان هذا القرآن على رأى النحويين

rows.speaker: ابن فارس
rows.claim: Ibn Faris calls this kind of ellipsis al-kaff.
rows.anchor: قال ابن فارس ويسمى هذا عند العرب الكف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The missing comparison after the question is indicated by the following woe for hardened hearts: is the one whose chest God opened like one whose heart hardened?
rows.anchor: وقد يومئ إلى المحذوف إما متأخر كقوله تعالى ﴿ أفمن شرح الله صدره للإسلام ﴾ فإنه لم يجئ له جواب فى اللفظ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An omitted preceding subject in the question about the devout worshipper is cued by the prior description of a person who calls on his Lord in distress.
rows.anchor: وإما متقدم كقوله تعالى ﴿ أم من هو قانت آناء الليل ﴾ فإنه أومأ إلى ما قبله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase about the promised Garden is another example where an omitted comparison or subject is supplied from surrounding words, including contrast with one who remains in the Fire.
rows.anchor: ونظيره ﴿ مثل الجنة التي وعد المتقون ﴾ ومن هذه صفته ﴿ كمن هو خالد في النار ﴾

rows.speaker: محمد بن كعب القرظي
rows.claim: Muhammad ibn Kaʿb al-Qurazi says the following verses explain al-samad: God neither begets nor is begotten and none is his equal.
rows.anchor: قال محمد بن كعب القرظي تفسيره ﴿ لم يلد ولم يولد

rows.speaker: أبو العالية
rows.claim: Abu al-ʿAliya says the following clauses explain haluʿ: a person despairs when harmed and withholds when blessed; Thaʿlab likewise says God has explained the word.
rows.anchor: قال أبو العالية تفسيره ﴿ إذا مسه الشر جزوعا وإذا مسه الخير منوعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The following mentions of Abraham's station and the safety of whoever enters the House explain the clear signs.
rows.anchor: مقام إبراهيم ومن دخله كان آمنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The general threat does not include Jesus and Ezra, whose immunity was clear; after the polytheists objected, the verse about those promised the good was revealed as an explicit exclusion.
rows.anchor: ومعلوم أنه لم يرد به المسيح وعزيرا فنزلت الآية مطلقة اكتفاء بالدلالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lightning means fear of thunderbolts and hope for rain; fear comes first because strikes occur at the first flash, while rain follows repeated flashes, so fear gives way to relief.
rows.anchor: تقديم الخوف على الطمع إذ كانت الصواعق تقع من أول برقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An objection asks how a following denial of two gods refutes three; the answer distinguishes saying our gods are three, which presupposes two, from saying we have three gods, where negation targets existence itself.
rows.anchor: فأجاب بأنه لا ينفيه ولكن يناقضه لأن تقدير آلهتنا ثلاثة يثبت وجود إلهين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author considers the proposed answers to those premises questionable.
rows.anchor: وفي أجوبة هذه المقدمات نظر

rows.speaker: ابن جني
rows.claim: Ibn Jinni analyzes the phrase as omitting the genitive construction, meaning third of three, as expressed elsewhere.
rows.anchor: وذكر ابن جني أن الآية من حذف المضاف أي ثالث ثلاثة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The predicate after wa-zilluha is omitted and understood as daʾim, lasting.
rows.anchor: نحو ﴿ أكلها دائم وظلها ﴾ 1 أي دائم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After naming the prophets, this is a reminder; after describing their Garden, this is signals the tyrants' fate, with the omitted predicate understood from context.
rows.anchor: فقال ﴿ هذا ذكر ﴾ 2 ثم لما ذكر مصيرهم إلى الجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The predicate and comparison are omitted: is one whose chest is opened better than one made constricted and hard-hearted? The following warning signals the contrast.
rows.anchor: أي أهذا خير أمن جعل صدره ضيقا حرجا وقسا قلبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They said no harm, with the complement left implicit.
rows.anchor: وقوله تعالى ﴿ قالوا لا ضير ﴾ 5

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning about seeing them panic with no escape is another example of an omitted clause.
rows.anchor: ولو ترى إذ فزعوا فلا فوت

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: Sibawayh says the thief's predicate is omitted, understood as in what I recite to you; fa-qtau is a separate sentence, as with the verse about adulterers.
rows.anchor: قال سيبويه الخبر 8 محذوف أي فيما أتلوه السارق والسارقة

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: Sibawayh gives the same omitted-predicate analysis for the verse about adulterers.
rows.anchor: وكذا قوله ﴿ الزانية والزاني ﴾ 9 فيما نقص لكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other grammarians take al-sariq as subject and fa-qtau as its predicate; its generic sense permits a fa-prefixed predicate like a conditional, while Sibawayh estimates ellipsis because the predicate is imperative.
rows.anchor: وقال غيره السارق مبتدأ فاقطعوا خبره وجاز ذلك لأن الاسم عام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reciters agree on nominative case although the preferred Arabic analogy is accusative; some read accusatively, but the general readers retained nominative.
rows.anchor: إجماع القراء على الرفع مع أن الأمر الاختياري فيه النصب

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: Sibawayh takes mithlu as the predicate of an omitted subject, meaning that what is recited is the likeness of the Garden promised to the God-fearing.
rows.anchor: مثل هنا خبر مبتدأ محذوف أي فيما نقض عليكم مثل الجنة

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: Sibawayh also treats the construction about the two who commit the act as relying on an omitted clause.
rows.anchor: وكذا قال أيضا في قوله تعالى ﴿ واللذان يأتيانها منكم فآذوهما ﴾ إنه على الإضمار
